stories.title_en: Overhearing the Official, Then Going Out to Swindle

paragraphs.zh: 里有寡婦，富蓋鄉鄰。止生一子甘澍，年方弱冠，恪守祖業，不敢生放。鄉人路五两問之借銀谷，皆不肯，心恨之。歸與妻胡氏謀，要賴他强姦。妻許曰：“可。”又托心友支九为干证，即往分巡道处告。道亲提审，先問胡氏曰：“甘澍因何到你家？”胡氏曰：“他家豪富，终日无图，只是姦淫人婦女。知我男人未在家，无故来调戏我；不从便强抱亲嘴，骂他不去。支九来邀我夫贩货，甘澍方走去。”再問支九：“你往路五家何干？”支九曰：“小的與路五都挑贩为生，因邀他买货，听得（里）面婦人喊骂，甘澍走出。”又問甘澍曰：“你因何與婦人角口？”甘澍曰：“并无到他家，哪有角口？問路五左右鄰便知。”左右鄰都称：“甘澍寡婦之子，素不敢非为。外间并未聞姦情，此是装情捏他。”路五执曰：“他万金巨富，岂不能买两个干证？”左右鄰曰：“我鄰近不知，他支九隔越一街，岂不是买来作证？”道曰：“路五贫民，何能买人作证？”将左右鄰并甘澍各责二十，定要問做强姦。甘澍出而惧甚，思无解释。
paragraphs.en: In the ward there was a widow, richer than the neighbors. She had only one son, Gan Shu, just of age, who kept to the family property and dared not lend at interest. A fellow villager, Lu Wu, asked him twice for a loan of silver and grain; both times he refused, and Lu hated him. Lu went home and plotted with his wife, née Hu, to frame Gan for rape. She agreed. He also enlisted a trusted friend, Zhi Jiu, as a witness, and they went to the circuit inspector’s office to file the charge. The inspector heard the case himself. He first asked Hu Shi, “Why did Gan Shu come to your house?” Hu Shi said, “His family is rich and idle all day; he only debauches other men’s women. He knew my husband was not at home, came for no reason to tease me; when I would not, he seized me and kissed me. I cursed him and he would not go. Zhi Jiu came to ask my husband to go trading, and only then did Gan Shu leave.” He asked Zhi Jiu, “What business had you at Lu Wu’s?” Zhi Jiu said, “I and Lu Wu both live by carrying goods to sell. I went to ask him to buy stock. I heard a woman inside shouting and cursing, and Gan Shu came out.” He asked Gan Shu, “Why did you quarrel with the woman?” Gan Shu said, “I never went to his house. How could there be a quarrel? Ask Lu Wu’s neighbors on either side and you will know.” The neighbors all said, “Gan Shu is a widow’s son and has never dared do wrong. We have heard of no adultery from outside; this is a cooked-up story to frame him.” Lu Wu insisted, “He is worth ten thousand in gold. How could he not buy two witnesses?” The neighbors said, “We live next door and know nothing. Zhi Jiu lives a street away. Is he not a bought witness?” The inspector said, “Lu Wu is a poor man. How could he buy witnesses?” He had the neighbors and Gan Shu each beaten twenty strokes, and was determined to convict rape. Gan Shu came out badly frightened, and could think of no way out.

paragraphs.zh: 晚堂退后，道已封门，在后堂周旋闲行，沉默思想，忽自言曰：“错矣！错矣！”又周行数次，遂拂衣而入。适有防夫涂山，在外窥道举动，聞其言错，想必是审此姦情一事也。夤夜越墙而出，扣甘澍歇家门。歇家开门延入。甘澍正忧闷无计。涂山曰：“你今日事要关节否？”澍曰：“甚关节可解？正要求之。”涂山曰：“道爷适有妻舅到，三日内即要打发起身，唯此最灵。若投他，明日即复审，更大胜矣。”澍曰：“如此得可好。须銀几何？”涂山曰：“此翻自案事，不比别人情，须百金方可。”澍曰：“百金我出，只要明日复审。”涂山曰：“舅爷今酒席尚未散，吾当即入言之。”澍與歇家送出。道大门已封，涂山复从居旁民家越墙而入。
paragraphs.en: After the evening session the inspector had already sealed the gates. He paced in the rear hall, thinking in silence, then suddenly said to himself, “Wrong! Wrong!” He walked around several more times, then shook out his sleeves and went in. It happened that a watchman, Tu Shan, was outside watching the inspector’s movements. Hearing him say “wrong,” he guessed it must be this rape case. In the dead of night he climbed the wall, went out, and knocked at the inn where Gan Shu was staying. The innkeeper opened and let him in. Gan Shu was sitting worried, with no plan. Tu Shan said, “For today’s business, do you want a private channel?” Shu said, “What channel would clear it? That is just what I need.” Tu Shan said, “His Honor the inspector happens to have a wife’s brother visiting. In three days he must be sent off. This is the most effective route. If you go through him, there will be a rehearing tomorrow, and you will win still more.” Shu said, “If that works, good. How much silver?” Tu Shan said, “This is a matter on his own docket, not like an ordinary favor. It will take a hundred taels.” Shu said, “I will put up a hundred taels, so long as there is a rehearing tomorrow.” Tu Shan said, “The uncle’s feast has not yet broken up. I will go in and speak at once.” Shu and the innkeeper saw him out. The inspector’s main gate was already sealed; Tu Shan again climbed the wall through a neighboring house and went in.

paragraphs.zh: 次日，道出早堂，即出牌复审强姦事。甘澍大喜，以为果验也。下午再审甘澍曰：“路五曾問你措借否？”澍曰：“他两次問借銀谷，我皆不肯，因此仇恨，妆情诬我。”再审胡氏曰：“甘澍未到你家，哪有强姦事？将拶起！”路五边未用銀，一拶即紧。胡氏难忍，即吐实“未有强姦。只措借不肯，故妆情告他。”又将路五、支九各打三十，将甘澍全解无罪。涂山即跟出索銀。甘澍曰：“吾乐與之。”涂山自索谢，澍另以十两與之。涂山以銀入道卸起，再出索添谢，又得十两。当时以舅爷关节之力，岂知出道之自悔，而銀尽为涂山所风騙乎！
paragraphs.en: The next day the inspector held morning court and at once issued a slip for a rehearing of the rape case. Gan Shu was overjoyed, thinking it had indeed taken effect. In the afternoon Gan Shu was examined again: “Did Lu Wu ever press you for a loan?” Shu said, “Twice he asked to borrow silver and grain; I refused both times. That is why he hates me and cooked up this charge.” Hu Shi was examined again: “Gan Shu never came to your house. How could there be a rape? Bring the finger-squeezers!” Lu Wu’s side had spent no silver; the squeezers were tightened at once. Hu Shi could not bear it and told the truth: “There was no rape. He would not lend, so we cooked up a charge.” Lu Wu and Zhi Jiu were each given thirty strokes, and Gan Shu was fully cleared as not guilty. Tu Shan followed him out to demand the silver. Gan Shu said, “I am glad to give it.” Tu Shan took his own thank-you; Shu gave him another ten taels besides. Tu Shan took the silver into the yamen, put it away, came out again to demand more thanks, and got another ten taels. At the time they thought it was the power of the uncle’s private channel. How were they to know it came from the inspector’s own second thoughts, and that all the silver had been pocketed by Tu Shan as a windfall swindle?

paragraphs.zh: 按：衙役皆以騙养身供家，丰衣足食，其騙何可枚举！蓋事事是騙，日日是騙，人人是騙。虽罄南山竹，何能悉之；虽包拯再生，何能察之？予素不入公庭，此中情弊，希所知聞。此其偶得于真见者，故述其弊窦如此。然衙中虽人人是姦徒，事事是騙薮，吾唯早完公课，百忍不讼，虽贪吏悍卒，其如我何！故曰：机虽巧，不蹈为高；鸩虽毒，不饮为高；衙役虽騙，不入为高。纵有无妄之灾，必有明官能昭雪之者。何也？官皆读书人，明者多而昏者少也。无奈在衙人役，各以阴云霾雾蔽之耳。故唯忍小忿，不入衙为高也。
paragraphs.en: Note: Yamen runners all live by swindling, to keep their families in ample clothes and food. How can their swindles be counted one by one? For every affair is a swindle, every day is a swindle, every person is a swindle. Even if you used up the bamboos of the southern hills, you could not set them all down; even if Bao Zheng were born again, he could not see through them. I have never been one to enter a public court; of the tricks inside I have heard little. This I happened to see for myself, so I record the opening as it was. Yet though every man in a yamen is a knave and every affair a nest of swindles, if I only pay my public dues early and endure a hundred wrongs rather than sue, then greedy clerks and fierce soldiers can do nothing to me. So it is said: a trap may be clever—the high thing is not to step in it; a poison may be deadly—the high thing is not to drink it; yamen runners may swindle—the high thing is not to go in. Even if some undeserved disaster comes, there will surely be a clear-eyed official to right it. Why? Officials are all men who have read books; the clear ones are many and the muddled few. The trouble is only that the men serving in the yamen screen them with dark cloud and fog. So the high thing is to swallow small anger and not enter a yamen.

stories.title_en: Drafting a Heavy Sentence on Purpose to Free a Prisoner

paragraphs.zh: 富民元植者，家温行谨，奕世良善，偶與鄉权贵有隙。鄉贵素善叶推官，乃吹毛求疵，砌元植之恶十餘件。叶推官为之送访，按院即批與叶审。叶提元植，谕之曰：“汝之恶迹，我已备晓，罪在有定。只汝家殷富，不許央关节。若有关节，罪有加无减。且收入监，候拘到被害，即听审定罪。”叶推官素廉正，从来不纳分上。今元植既承面诫，越不敢展转，只惶惧待罪耳。
paragraphs.en: A well-off commoner named Yuan Zhi was comfortable in his means and careful in his conduct, of a line of decent people for generations. He happened to have a quarrel with a powerful man of the district. That man had long been on good terms with Assistant Prefect Ye, so he picked bones and piled up more than ten charges of Yuan Zhi’s “evils.” Assistant Prefect Ye sent them up as an investigation; the touring censor then assigned the case to Ye. Ye had Yuan Zhi brought in and told him, “I already know your misdeeds in full; the punishment is fixed. Your family is rich: you are not to send private appeals. If there is a private appeal, the punishment will be increased, not reduced. Put him in jail. When the alleged victims have been summoned, we will hear the case and pass sentence.” Assistant Prefect Ye had always been honest and never took a word from anyone. Yuan Zhi, having been warned to his face, still less dared to stir, and only waited in fear for punishment.

paragraphs.zh: 适眷亲易鄉官，素與植相善，知其事属仇陷，默地代诉于太府，托转释于四尊。太府乘间缓颊及之。叶四尊大怒，歸取元植，责之曰：“我叫你不得投分上，反央太爷来讲。这样刁恶人，定要拟你谪戍！”元植茫不知来历，叩头曰：“老爷素不纳关节，一府通知；又蒙钧旨面谕，怎敢央太爷？实不知事从何来。”叶爷曰：“且入监去，定是军罪。”元植出查，方知事出易鄉官，自以己意代释，并不使植知也。植思无处可解，寻其用事凌书手，密商曰：“能为我减军入徒，当以厚礼谢。”凌书曰：“能出百金，为汝计之。”植許曰：“可。”以銀封讫。
paragraphs.en: It happened that a kinsman, retired official Yi, had long been friendly with Zhi. Knowing the matter was an enemy’s trap, he quietly spoke for him to the prefect, asking the prefect to pass a word to the Fourth Lord (Ye) for a release. The prefect found an opening and eased the matter along. Fourth Lord Ye was furious. He had Yuan Zhi brought back and rebuked him: “I told you not to send in a word, and you instead got His Honor the prefect to speak. A vicious man like you—I am determined to sentence you to frontier military exile!” Yuan Zhi had no idea where this had come from. He kowtowed: “Your Honor never takes private channels; the whole prefecture knows it. And I was ordered to my face. How would I dare send the prefect? I truly do not know how this arose.” Lord Ye said, “Go back into jail. It will certainly be a military sentence.” Yuan Zhi came out and inquired, and only then learned it had come from retired official Yi, who of his own accord had spoken for a release without letting Zhi know. Zhi could think of no way out. He sought out Ling, the clerk who handled the work, and said in private, “If you can get my military exile reduced to penal servitude, I will thank you richly.” Clerk Ling said, “If you can put up a hundred taels, I will manage it for you.” Zhi agreed, and sealed up the silver.

paragraphs.zh: 叶爷果唤凌书手作招曰：“须寻一军律拟来。”凌书故以绞罪拟上。叶爷命改招，只可拟军。凌书过一日再以绞罪拟曰：“访单中惟謀死亲弟一件最重，正合绞罪。餘某条某条，只是徒罪，并无合军律者。”叶爷寻思：“有对头之状，尚不轻入人绞，况是拿访，而可绞人？”曰：“造化了他，只拟徒罢。”后拟上三年徒。元植欣然纳赎，凌书遂安受百金之贿。在叶爷，宁知其外受金而内拟人重罪乎？故衙役之欺官，虽神君不及察也。
paragraphs.en: Lord Ye did in fact call Clerk Ling to draft the confession-and-sentence: “Find a military statute and propose it.” Ling deliberately proposed strangulation. Lord Ye ordered the draft changed: only military exile could be proposed. A day later Ling again proposed strangulation: “On the investigation list, the heaviest item is plotting the death of a younger brother, which exactly fits strangulation. The other articles are only penal servitude; none fits a military statute.” Lord Ye thought: “Even on a complaint from an enemy I would not lightly send a man to the silk cord; still less on a picked-up investigation.” He said, “His luck. Just propose penal servitude.” In the end it was three years’ servitude. Yuan Zhi gladly paid the redemption; Clerk Ling quietly took the hundred-tael bribe. As for Lord Ye, how was he to know that outside someone had taken gold, and inside a heavier crime had been proposed against the man? So when yamen clerks cheat an official, even a spirit-like magistrate cannot see it.

paragraphs.zh: 按：善有旌奖，恶有拿访，此朝廷激劝一大机权也。今旌者多由攒刺之巧，访者或由权贵之嗾，其虚实益相半耳。然犹幸有拿访一途，可以少惕刁顽，稍为良民吐气。特被访者出入于問官之心，高下于权书之手，其情得罪当者亦少矣。当官持权者，或遇大故重情，必虚心详审，明察沉断，庶可杜姦欺之一二耳。
paragraphs.en: Note: The good are commended, the bad are seized and investigated: this is a great engine of the court for urging and warning. Today those commended often get there by clever self-promotion, and those investigated are sometimes set on by the powerful; truth and falsehood are about half and half. Still we are lucky to have investigation at all, which can somewhat cow the cunning and let decent people breathe a little. Only, those investigated rise and fall in the examining official’s mind and are raised or lowered in the powerful clerk’s hand; few in fact get the punishment they deserve. Those who hold office and wield power, when they meet a grave matter with heavy consequences, must empty their minds, examine in detail, look clearly and decide firmly; only then can they block one or two of the frauds.

stories.title_en: A Clerk Scolds a Convict in Order to Split the Beating

paragraphs.zh: 传包孝肃为官，清廉明察，用法无私，诈不得以巧辨售，罪不得以权贵免，又不纳分上。故人称之曰：“关节不到，有阎罗包老。”
paragraphs.en: It is told that when Bao Xiaosu was in office he was clean, clear-eyed, and used the law without private feeling. Trickery could not sell itself by clever argument; punishment could not be escaped by powerful connections; and he took no private word. So people said of him, “Where no private channel can reach, there is Yama Bao.”

paragraphs.zh: 适有富豪子犯姦情真，知难逃洞察，预與一老胥謀曰：“包爷精明，察事如神。我所犯情真，干证又直证，罪实难逃。若重罚犹可输纳；唯痛责实是难堪。有何计可以减责，必不惜厚费图之。”老胥曰：“明日若当责时，你奔近案前，强辩求申。我从旁呵斥，为你分责，或可减你一半。此外，别无策可图也。”
paragraphs.en: A rich man’s son was truly guilty of an illicit affair. Knowing he could not escape the clear eye, he plotted in advance with an old clerk: “Lord Bao is sharp and sees a case like a spirit. What I did is true, and the witnesses testify straight; the punishment can hardly be avoided. A heavy fine I could still pay; only a painful beating would be hard to bear. If there is any plan to reduce the beating, I will not begrudge a thick fee to work it.” The old clerk said, “Tomorrow, when the beating is due, run up to the bench and argue hard for a hearing. I will shout you down from the side and take part of the beating for you; perhaps your half can be cut. Beyond that there is no plan.”

paragraphs.zh: 次日，包公审得真情，发怒要打富子四十。富子奔近案（前），哓哓申辩不已。老胥从旁大声呵之曰：“速去受责，何须許多说话，罪岂赦你！”包公见之，大恨此吏揽权起威，恐后日窃势騙人，外必生事，即先责老胥二十板，偏减去富子二十，欲使威不自胥出，不知正落其謀中也。老胥遂得厚赂，而包公漠不知之。
paragraphs.en: The next day Lord Bao found the facts true, grew angry, and was going to give the rich son forty strokes. The rich son ran up to the bench and argued on and on. The old clerk shouted loudly from the side, “Go and take your beating at once! Why so much talk? Will the punishment be remitted for you?” Lord Bao saw this and hated the clerk for seizing power and putting on airs. He feared that later the man would steal influence to swindle people and make trouble outside, so he first beat the old clerk twenty strokes and, of all things, took twenty off the rich son, wanting the awe not to seem to come from the clerk—not knowing he had fallen right into the plot. The old clerk then got a thick bribe, and Lord Bao knew nothing of it.

paragraphs.zh: 按：吏为姦，皆是知本官性情，而变幻用之。老胥知包公严明，岂容胥吏招权？故旁呵犯人，包公必责吏而故恕犯人，以见胥吏之无权，欲外人不畏慑之。岂知于难减责之中，故分责以取其贿，又孰从而察之？公且受胥騙，况后之为官者哉！
paragraphs.en: Note: When clerks work fraud, they all know their superior’s temper and twist it to use. The old clerk knew Lord Bao was strict and clear, and would never let a clerk gather power. So he shouted at the prisoner from the side: Lord Bao was bound to beat the clerk and deliberately spare the prisoner, to show that clerks have no power, and so that people outside would not stand in awe of them. Who would have thought that, in a beating that could hardly be reduced, he would split the beating in order to take a bribe—and who would see through it? Even his lordship was swindled by a clerk; how much more those who hold office after him!
